## Statement

Assume AC. Use the type-H prior of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], retaining its original conditions: $1/2<\alpha\le1$, $f_0\in C^\alpha([0,1])$, $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, either original cutoff $L_n=j_n$ or $L_n=\ell_n$, and $c_1 2^{-L_na}\le a_{k,L_n}\le c_2$ for fixed positive $a,c_1,c_2$. Write $m_n=2^{L_n}$. In the Haar convention, the scaling function is $1$, the detail functions are
$$\psi_{lk}=2^{l/2}(\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k}}-\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k+1}}),\qquad l\ge0,\quad 0\le k<2^l,$$
and a histogram at resolution $L_n$ has only the scaling coordinate and levels $l<L_n$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID from $f_0$, let $N_{nk}=\sum_i\mathbf1_{I_{L_n,k}}(X_i)$, and define the empirical histogram
$$h_n(x)=m_n N_{nk}/n\quad\text{on }I_{L_n,k}.$$
Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$ be the density posterior for the stated histogram prior. For every nondecreasing $w_l\ge1$ with $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, its conditional law $Q_n$ of $\sqrt n(f-h_n)$ satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}(Q_n,\mathcal L(G_{P_0}))\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where the Borel centered Gaussian bridge $G_{P_0}$ is supplied by [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]] and has covariance $P_0[(\psi-P_0\psi)(\psi'-P_0\psi')]$. Its scaling coordinate is zero. This proves the type-H source-specific posterior BvM with the empirical projection center; no additional contraction, bias, or Dirichlet-parameter condition is imposed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the original type-H truth, cutoff, parameter, Haar, observation, and admissible-weight conditions in the Statement.

[F1] [[lem-finite-dirichlet-gamma-representation-and-bernstein-bound]]: a Dirichlet vector of shapes $\beta_k$ is $Z_k/S$ for independent Gamma$(\beta_k,1)$ variables; $S$ has mean and variance $B=\sum_k\beta_k$. For $T(q)=\sum_kq_k(Z_k-\beta_k)$, $|q_k|\le b$, and $V=\sum_k\beta_kq_k^2>0$, $\Pr(|T(q)|>x)\le2e^{-x^2/[2(V+bx)]}$. Disjoint Gamma shapes add, and $\mathbb E e^{uZ_k}=(1-u)^{-\beta_k}$ for $u<1$.

[F2] [[thm-dirichlet-multinomial-conjugate-update]] and [[thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels]] identify the positive finite normalized Dirichlet likelihood update.

[F3] [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]] supplies the Borel Gaussian bridge law for the bounded density in the Statement.

[F4] [[lem-m0w-finite-projection-and-tail-bvm-criterion]] concludes BL convergence from every fixed finite-coordinate BL limit and vanishing posterior tails in the iterated limit.

[F5] [[thm-prokhorov-tightness-theorem-on-polish-spaces]] gives subsequential weak compactness of tight finite-dimensional Borel laws under AC; [[lem-uniqueness-of-a-multivariate-exponential-transform]] identifies finite laws with a common moment-generating transform near zero.

[F6] [[thm-vector-slutsky]] passes a finite-dimensional weak limit through algebraic operations with quantities converging in probability to constants. [[lem-bounded-lipschitz-metric-characterizes-weak-convergence-on-polish-spaces]] converts finite-dimensional weak convergence to BL convergence.

[F7] [[cor-markov-inequality-for-random-variables]] and [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]] give moment, exponential, and union bounds.

[F8] [[lem-type-s-h-prior-draws-are-l2-densities]] supplies the finite histogram density construction. [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]] supplies the coefficient norm and admissibility convention, with the finite scaling coordinate included.

## Proof

**Given:** All hypotheses in the Statement, with full AC throughout.

1.1 Abbreviate $m=m_n$, $a_k=a_{k,L_n}$, $A=\sum_ka_k$, $\beta_k=N_{nk}+a_k$, and $B=n+A$. The original cutoff conditions and $\alpha>1/2$ give $m/\sqrt n\to0$ and $m\log n/n\to0$, and $A\le c_2m$. On the positive simplex, the full-data histogram likelihood is $m^n\prod_k\omega_k^{N_{nk}}$. Multiplication by the prior density yields a constant times $\prod_k\omega_k^{\beta_k-1}$, with every shape positive; its normalization is finite positive by [F2]. Therefore the full-data posterior is Dirichlet$(\beta_k)_k$, regardless of whether the actual sampling truth is itself a histogram. By [F1] realize it by $\omega_k=Z_k/S$. Write $R_n$ for the posterior mean histogram measure, identified with its density in coefficient differences, with cell masses $\beta_k/B$. For a cell-constant function $q$, set $T(q)=\sum_kq_k(Z_k-\beta_k)$. Direct subtraction gives $\sqrt n(\omega q-R_nq)=(\sqrt n/S)T(q-R_nq)$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 Fix constants $t>0$ and $C$ large enough that $c:=tC-D_0(e^t-1)>0$. Since $N_{nk}$ is Binomial$(n,p_k)$ with $p_k=P_0I_{L_n,k}\le D_0/m$, independence of the observations gives $\mathbb E e^{tN_{nk}}=(1+p_k(e^t-1))^n\le e^{nD_0(e^t-1)/m}$. Hence $E_n=\{\max_kN_{nk}\le Cn/m\}$ satisfies $P_0^n(E_n^c)\le m e^{-cn/m}\to0$, by exponential Markov and the union bound. On $E_n$, for all sufficiently large $n$, $\beta_k\le C'n/m$, $B\le2n$, and both the empirical histogram density and the mean histogram density are bounded by a fixed constant $C'$ independent of $n$. [F7, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 On $E_n$, take any Haar detail $\psi=\psi_{lk}$ with $l<L_n$ and put $q=\psi-R_n\psi$. Then $|q|\le2\,2^{l/2}$ and $V=\sum_k\beta_kq_k^2=B\operatorname{Var}_{R_n}(\psi)\le B R_n\psi^2\le C'n$, using $\int\psi^2=1$ and the density bound. By [F1] and [F7], $\Pr(S<B/2\mid X^n)\le4/B$, because $\operatorname{Var}(S)=B$. On the complement, step 1.1 yields $|\sqrt n(\omega\psi-R_n\psi)|\le2|T(q)|/\sqrt n$. Thus, apart from the single event $\{S<B/2\}$, the conditional probability that this absolute coefficient exceeds $x$ is at most $2\exp\{-c_0x^2/(1+2^{l/2}x/\sqrt n)\}$ for a fixed $c_0>0$. The zero-variance case has no such failure event, by [F1]. [F1, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra, cases]

2.2 Choose a fixed $K>0$ sufficiently large. Uniformly over $l<L_n$, $2^{l/2}K\sqrt{l+1}/\sqrt n\le K\sqrt{m(L_n+1)/n}\to0$. Summing the exponential bounds of step 2.1 over levels $J<l<L_n$ and their $2^l$ coefficients therefore gives, for all large $n$, $\Pi_n\{\max_{J<l<L_n,k}|\sqrt n(f-R_n)_{lk}|/\sqrt{l+1}>K\mid X^n\}\le4/B+\sum_{l>J}2^{l+1}e^{-c_1K^2(l+1)}$ on $E_n$, with fixed $c_1>0$. The probability $4/B$ is counted only once, since the same $S$ normalizes every coordinate. Choose $K$ with $c_1K^2>2\log2$; the displayed series tail then tends to zero with $J$. For any $\varepsilon>0$, admissibility gives $K\sqrt{l+1}\le\varepsilon w_l$ for all sufficiently large $l$. Both $f$ and $R_n$ are histograms, so all their detail coordinates at $l\ge L_n$ vanish. Consequently their conditional $M(w)$ tails vanish in the iterated limit of [F4], first $n\to\infty$, then $J\to\infty$, since $P_0^n(E_n^c)\to0$. [F4, F7, F8, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 For a Haar detail $\psi=\psi_{lk}$, exact subtraction gives $\sqrt n(R_n\psi-P_n\psi)=\sqrt n[\sum_ka_k\psi_k-A P_n\psi]/B$. Haar cell values satisfy $m^{-1}\sum_k|\psi_k|=\int|\psi|=2^{-l/2}\le1$. Hence $|\sum_ka_k\psi_k|\le c_2m$, while on $E_n$, $|P_n\psi|\le C\int|\psi|\le C$. This bounds every such mean shift by $C''m/\sqrt n\to0$. The scaling-coordinate shift is exactly zero, and all coordinates at $l\ge L_n$ vanish for both centers. Since $w_l\ge1$, $\|\sqrt n(R_n-h_n)\|_{M(w)}\to0$ uniformly on $E_n$. In particular step 2.2 also supplies the required posterior tails about $h_n$. [F8, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

3.1 Fix finitely many Haar coordinates. Choose a fixed coarse dyadic partition of $r$ cells on which all their functions are constant. For large $n$ its cells are unions of level-$L_n$ cells. By [F1], the corresponding grouped Gamma variables $Z_{nj}$ are independent Gamma$(b_{nj},1)$ with $b_{nj}=N_n(J_j)+\sum_{I_{L_n,k}\subset J_j}a_k$. Their summed shape is still $B$. Write $p_j=P_0(J_j)>0$. Each coarse count satisfies $\mathbb E[N_n(J_j)/n]=p_j$ and variance at most $1/(4n)$, by observation independence. Markov applied to squared deviations, together with $A/n\to0$, proves $b_{nj}/n\to p_j$ in $P_0^n$-probability simultaneously for the fixed finite partition. [F1, F7, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.2 Consider any deterministic data sequence along which $b_{nj}/n\to p_j$ for every $j$. Under its conditional Gamma product laws put $Y_{nj}=(Z_{nj}-b_{nj})/\sqrt n$. For every fixed $t\in\mathbb R^r$, [F1] and the logarithm series give $\log\mathbb E e^{t\cdot Y_n}=\sum_j b_{nj}[-\log(1-t_j/\sqrt n)-t_j/\sqrt n]\to\tfrac12\sum_jp_jt_j^2$. The remainder is $O(n^{-3/2}\sum_jb_{nj}|t_j|^3)=O(n^{-1/2})$. The means of $Y_n$ are zero and their total second moments are $B/n=O(1)$, so their laws are tight by the squared-norm Markov bound and compactness of finite-dimensional closed balls. By [F5], any subsequence has a further weak limit. For any fixed $t$, the same expansion at $2t$ uniformly bounds $\mathbb E e^{2t\cdot Y_n}$; hence $e^{t\cdot Y_n}$ is uniformly integrable. Truncation of this continuous exponential therefore passes its expectation through each weakly convergent subsequence. The limit law has transform $\exp(\tfrac12\sum_jp_jt_j^2)$ and an exponential moment on a neighborhood of zero: $e^{\delta\sum_j|y_j|}\le\sum_{\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}^r}e^{\delta\epsilon\cdot y}$ and the corresponding transforms are finite. The independent centered normal vector with variances $p_j$ has this same transform, by completing the square in each normal density. Transform uniqueness [F5] identifies every subsequential limit, proving $Y_n\Rightarrow N_r(0,\operatorname{diag}(p))$. [F1, F5, F7, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 Here $(S-B)/\sqrt n=\sum_jY_{nj}$, $S/n\to1$ in conditional probability by its variance $B/n^2\to0$ and mean $B/n\to1$. Exact algebra gives $\sqrt n(Z_{nj}/S-b_{nj}/B)=(n/S)[Y_{nj}-(b_{nj}/B)\sum_hY_{nh}]$. By [F6] and step 3.2, this vector converges to $(U_j-p_j\sum_hU_h)_j$, with $U_j$ independent $N(0,p_j)$. Its covariance is $\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^T$. Applying the fixed linear map from coarse-cell masses to the chosen Haar coordinates yields covariance exactly $P_0[(\psi-P_0\psi)(\psi'-P_0\psi')]$. Step 2.3 removes the mean shift from $R_n$ to $h_n$ on $E_n$. Thus along every deterministic data sequence with the ratios in step 3.1 converging and $E_n$ eventually occurring, the finite-coordinate posterior converges weakly, hence in BL by [F6], to the corresponding projection of [F3]. [F3, F6, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

3.4 The preceding deterministic-sequence conclusion implies the finite-coordinate BL convergence in $P_0^n$-probability. To see this without a simultaneous conditional null-set assertion, if that convergence failed, there would be $\varepsilon,\eta>0$ and infinitely many $n$ with probability at least $\eta$ that the distance exceeds $\varepsilon$. Along a subsequence, step 3.1 and $P_0^n(E_n^c)\to0$ make the probability of a ratio error above $1/q$ or $E_n^c$ smaller than $\eta/2$ at its $q$th chosen index. Thus at each such index there exists data with distance above $\varepsilon$, ratio error below $1/q$, and $E_n$ true. AC selects a deterministic sequence of those data, contradicting step 3.3. This proves the asserted convergence in probability for each fixed finite projection. [F6, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 3.3, given, choose, contradiction]

4.1 The posterior histogram construction [F8] and its finite-dimensional simplex kernel make $Q_n$ a data-indexed Borel probability on $M_0(w)$: each draw and $h_n$ has only finitely many Haar coefficients, and its map from simplex coordinates is continuous. The target is the Borel bridge law [F3]. Step 3.4 supplies every fixed finite-projection BL limit, and steps 2.2–2.3 supply its posterior-tail condition. Apply [F4] to obtain the stated $M_0(w)$ BL convergence. Every original type-H assumption has been retained; in particular the lower parameter bound is compatible with, but is not needed beyond, positivity in this conjugate proof. [F3, F4, F8, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.4, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the S-regular wavelet basis in [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]], with $2^l$ coefficients at each level $l\ge0$. For $\alpha>0$, put $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and let the prior on $f=\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ have IID coefficients $\xi_{lk}$ with density $\varphi$. Assume countable choice for the $L^2$ prior construction supplied by [[lem-wavelet-product-prior-is-l2-valued]], and take the full posterior kernel as the supplied model input of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $f_0\in L^2([0,1])$, write $\theta_{0,lk}=\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle$ and $r_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}/\sigma_l$, and suppose

$$\sup_{l,k}|r_{lk}|\le M<\tau,$$

where $\varphi$ is a probability density satisfying $\varphi(u)\le C_\varphi$ for every $u$, $\varphi(u)\ge c_\varphi>0$ for $|u|<\tau$, $\int u^2\varphi(u)\,du<\infty$, and $\varphi$ is continuous at each $r_{lk}$. The observation model is

$$dX^{(n)}(t)=f_0(t)\,dt+n^{-1/2}dW(t),\qquad 0\le t\le1,$$

with standard white noise $W$; in the stated basis this is the sequence experiment $X_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}+n^{-1/2}Z_{lk}$ with independent standard normal coordinates. Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)$ be the product-coordinate posterior of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $N$ be the law of the canonical white noise in $H(\delta)$ and define

$$\widetilde\Pi_n:=\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)\circ[f\mapsto\sqrt n(f-X)]^{-1},\qquad \beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\mu,\nu):=\sup_{\substack{\|g\|_\infty\le1\\ \operatorname{Lip}_{H(\delta)}(g)\le1}}\left|\int g\,d\mu-\int g\,d\nu\right|.$$

For every $\delta>1/2$,

$$\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,N)\longrightarrow0$$

in probability under the true white-noise law $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$. This is a bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM conclusion; it asserts neither total-variation convergence on all Borel subsets nor an $L^2$-valued Gaussian limit.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]: $H(\delta)$ has norm $\|u\|_{H(\delta)}^2=\sum_{l,k}w_l^\delta|u_{lk}|^2$, where $w_l^\delta=a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}$, and its trace sum is finite for $\delta>1/2$.

[F2] [[lem-wavelet-product-prior-is-l2-valued]]: The product prior series defines an $L^2$-valued random element for $\alpha>0$ and finite coefficient second moment.

[F3] [[lem-white-noise-is-borel-gaussian-on-negative-sobolev-space]]: The canonical white-noise coefficient sequence has Borel Gaussian law $N$ on $H(\delta)$ for $\delta>1/2$, is not $L^2$-valued, and satisfies $\mathbb E\|W\|_{H(\delta')}^2=\sum_{l,k}w_l^{\delta'}<\infty$ for every $\delta'>1/2$.

[F4] [[lem-product-prior-posterior-second-moment-in-negative-sobolev-space]]: For any $\delta'>1/2$, $n\,\mathbb E_{f_0}^{(n)}\int\|f-f_0\|_{H(\delta')}^2\,\Pi_n(df\mid X)$ is bounded uniformly in $n$.

[F5] [[lem-finite-coordinate-posterior-total-variation-limit]]: For every fixed finite coordinate projection, the posterior and standard Gaussian densities of $\sqrt n(\theta_J-X_J)$ converge in $L^1$ in probability.

[F6] [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]: A supplied posterior kernel has product-coordinate marginals with densities proportional to $e^{-n(\theta_j-X_j)^2/2}\sigma_j^{-1}\varphi(\theta_j/\sigma_j)$.

[F7] [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-for-random-variables]]: On any probability space, $\mathbb E|UV|\le(\mathbb EU^2)^{1/2}(\mathbb EV^2)^{1/2}$ for square-integrable real random variables.

[F8] [[cor-markov-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For nonnegative $Y$ and $a>0$, $\mathbb P(Y\ge a)\le\mathbb E[Y]/a$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable choice supplies the $L^2$ prior construction and the density normal-law interface used by [F3]. The full posterior kernel is supplied as model input by [F6]; the posterior moment estimate, finite-coordinate convergence, and projection/tail inequalities introduce no further choice axiom.

**Given:** Countable choice, the basis, prior, truth, density conditions, white-noise experiment, and the supplied posterior kernel of [F6]. The stated bounded-Lipschitz convergence is proved below without using full AC.

## Proof

1.1 Fix $\delta>1/2$ and choose $\delta'$ with $1/2<\delta'<\delta$. Let $P_J$ retain all wavelet coordinates with level $l\le J$. Since $w_l^\delta/w_l^{\delta'}=(\log a_l)^{-2(\delta-\delta')}$ and $a_l\to\infty$, for $q_J:=(\log a_{J+1})^{-(\delta-\delta')}$ one has $\|(I-P_J)u\|_{H(\delta)}\le q_J\|u\|_{H(\delta')}\quad\text{and}\quad q_J\to0.$ For any probability law $Q$ on $H(\delta)$, coupling $U$ with $P_JU$ and using the defining Lipschitz bound gives $\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(Q,Q\circ P_J^{-1})\le\int\|(I-P_J)u\|_{H(\delta)}\,Q(du)$. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 For a fixed $J$, the middle term in $\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,N)\le\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,\widetilde\Pi_n\circ P_J^{-1})+\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n\circ P_J^{-1},N\circ P_J^{-1})+\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(N\circ P_J^{-1},N)$ tends to zero in probability: [F5] gives $L^1$ convergence of the projected posterior and Gaussian coordinate densities. Every bounded-Lipschitz test function restricted to the projected subspace is bounded by $1$, so its integral difference is at most that $L^1$ distance. [F5, algebra]

1.3 The last term is bounded by $\mathbb E\|W-P_JW\|_{H(\delta)}$, which is at most $\bigl(\mathbb E\|W-P_JW\|_{H(\delta)}^2\bigr)^{1/2}=\bigl(\sum_{l>J,k}w_l^\delta\bigr)^{1/2}$ by [F3] and [F7]. This tends to zero as $J\to\infty$ by [F1]. [F1, F3, F7, algebra]

2.1 Under the joint true-data/posterior law, using the supplied posterior model [F6] and the $L^2$ prior construction [F2], $U=\sqrt n(f-X)=\sqrt n(f-f_0)-W$, where $W=\sqrt n(X-f_0)$ has law $N$. By [F4], [F3] and $(a-b)^2\le2a^2+2b^2$, $\mathbb E_{f_0}^{(n)}\int\|U\|_{H(\delta')}^2\,\Pi_n(df\mid X)\le2n\mathbb E_{f_0}^{(n)}\int\|f-f_0\|_{H(\delta')}^2\,\Pi_n(df\mid X)+2\mathbb E\|W\|_{H(\delta')}^2\le C,$ with $C$ independent of $n$. Applying [F7] under the posterior probability and then under the true-data probability, together with step 1.1, gives $\mathbb E_{f_0}^{(n)}\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,\widetilde\Pi_n\circ P_J^{-1})\le q_J\sqrt C.$ Thus the first projection error can be made uniformly small by taking $J$ large. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Fix $0<\varepsilon<1$ and choose $J$ so the expected first and deterministic third terms are each less than $\varepsilon^2$. By [F8], the probability that the first term exceeds $\varepsilon$ is at most $\varepsilon$; the deterministic third term is less than $\varepsilon$. For this fixed $J$, step 1.2 makes the probability that the middle term exceeds $\varepsilon$ tend to zero. The triangle bound then gives a limiting upper bound $\varepsilon$ for the probability that the full distance exceeds $3\varepsilon$. Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, $\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,N)\to0$ in $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$-probability. [F8, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$ be measurable spaces and let $y\mapsto\Pi_y$ be a supplied posterior probability kernel. For $\alpha\in[0,1]$, a set-valued rule $C$ is **graph-measurable** when
$$\{(y,\theta)\in\mathsf Y\times\Theta:\theta\in C(y)\}\in\mathcal Y\otimes\mathcal T.$$
It is a **posterior credible set at level $1-\alpha$** when it is graph-measurable and
$$\Pi_y(C(y))\ge 1-\alpha\qquad\text{for every }y\text{ in its declared data domain}.$$
The posterior-mass function is measurable by integration of the indicator of the membership graph against the kernel. If a density is available relative to a specified dominating measure, a highest-posterior-density region selects parameter values with largest density; such regions need not be intervals and may be disconnected or nonunique.

Let $\pi$ be a prior probability on $(E,\mathcal S)$ and let $Q:E\to T$ be a probability kernel dominated by a sigma-finite measure $\nu$ on $(T,\mathcal T)$, with specified nonnegative jointly measurable density $\ell:E\times T\to[0,\infty]$:
$$Q(\theta,B)=\int_B\ell(\theta,y)\,\nu(dy)\quad\text{for every }\theta\in E,\ B\in\mathcal T.$$

Define $m(y)=\int_E\ell(\theta,y)\,\pi(d\theta)$. Under the joint law with density $\ell$ relative to $\pi\times\nu$, a conditional law of the parameter given the observation is
$$K(y,A)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\int_A\ell(\theta,y)\,\pi(d\theta)}{m(y)},&0<m(y)<\infty,\\ \pi(A),&m(y)=0\text{ or }m(y)=\infty.\end{cases}$$

The observation marginal is $m\,d\nu$, and the filled fibres have marginal mass zero. This is a choice-free assertion about the explicit kernel and event identities.

derivations.claim: For data with $k$ successes, the likelihood is $\theta^k(1-\theta)^{n-k}$. It is bounded by $1$ and positive for $0<\theta<1$, so its integral against the uniform prior is finite and strictly positive. [F2] therefore gives the posterior density proportional to that likelihood. The sample space is finite for fixed $n$, so the interval rule's membership graph is a finite union of measurable slices. The posterior density is positive on $(0,1)$, making its CDF continuous and strictly increasing there; the posterior probability between its two quantiles is $(1-\alpha/2)-\alpha/2=1-\alpha$. Thus the rule is credible by [F1].

At $\theta_0=0$, the data are all zero with probability one, so the likelihood is $(1-\theta)^n$. Its normalizing integral is $\int_0^1(1-\theta)^n d\theta=1/(n+1)$, giving posterior density $(n+1)(1-\theta)^n$ and CDF $F_n(t)=1-(1-t)^{n+1}$. Solving $F_n(q_u)=u$ yields $q_u=1-(1-u)^{1/(n+1)}$. In particular $q_{\alpha/2}>0$, so $0\notin C_n$ for every $n$.

Because the truth is zero and all data are zero almost surely, [L1] gives frequentist coverage $P_0\{0\in C_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\}=0$. This contradicts the asserted lower bound $1-\alpha>0$ and exhibits failure at the boundary identified in [A1].

citations.quote: Assume countable choice. Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the wavelet or trigonometric basis from [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. Let $Z_{lk}$ be mutually independent real random variables with density $g(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$. Define the formal white-noise coefficient sequence $W=(Z_{lk})$. For every $\delta>1/2$, this sequence is almost surely an element of $H(\delta)$ and is a Borel Gaussian random element there. Its law $N$ is a Borel probability on $H(\delta)$. For an infinite-dimensional basis, white noise is not an $L^2([0,1])$-valued random element. Here Gaussian means that each continuous real linear functional has a centered law $N(0,v)$ in the density convention of [[lem-density-normal-laws-and-square-summable-gaussian-series]]; in particular, for $L(c)=\sum_jd_jc_j$ its variance is $\sum_jd_j^2$ whenever this pairing is continuous on $H(\delta)$.
Assume AC. A family $\mathcal A$ of Borel probabilities on a Polish space S is tight if and only if it is relatively sequentially compact for weak convergence.

A topological space is **Polish** when it is separable ([[def-separable-space]]) and completely metrizable: its topology is induced by some complete metric ([[lem-complete-remetrisation]]). No particular compatible complete metric or countable dense subset is part of the structure.

Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a countable complete orthonormal basis of the real Hilbert space $L^2([0,1])$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). For a wavelet basis, index levels by $l\ge0$, let $K_l$ have $2^l$ indices, and put $a_l=2^l$ for $l\ge1$ and $a_0=2$ for the finite coarsest level. This finite-level convention only prevents a zero logarithmic weight and does not change any convergence criterion below. For a trigonometric basis, use its integer frequency index $l$, bounded multiplicities, and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$.

Here an **$S$-regular wavelet basis** means a wavelet orthonormal basis whose members are $S$ times differentiable, with each derivative through order $S$ in $L^2([0,1])$, following the source convention. The weak BvM theorem below only uses the basis's completeness, orthonormality, and level counts.

For $\delta>0$, define $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ to be the space of coefficient sequences $c=(c_{lk})$ with norm

$$\|c\|_{H(\delta)}^2:=\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}|c_{lk}|^2<\infty.$$

Its inner product is the corresponding weighted coefficient inner product. Multiplying each coordinate by $a_l^{-1/2}(\log a_l)^{-\delta}$ identifies it isometrically with $\ell^2(I)$, where $I=\{(l,k):k\in K_l\}$ (or the corresponding trigonometric index set). This sequence space is complete: if $x^{(m)}$ is Cauchy, each coordinate converges to a scalar $x_i$; for every finite $F\subset I$, the Cauchy bound passes to the limit in $\sum_{i\in F}|x_i^{(m)}-x_i^{(n)}|^2$, so the supremum over finite $F$ shows $x^{(m)}\to x$ in $\ell^2(I)$. It is separable because finite-support sequences with rational coordinates form a countable dense set. Thus $H(\delta)$ is a separable Hilbert space without an additional choice assumption.

A function $f\in L^2([0,1])$ is identified with its coefficient sequence $c_{lk}=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$. For each finite set $F$ of indices, orthonormality makes $\sum_{(l,k)\in F}c_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ orthogonal to its residual in $L^2$, so the Pythagorean identity gives $\sum_F|c_{lk}|^2\le\|f\|_2^2$. Taking the supremum over finite $F$ and using the boundedness of the weights proves continuity of the coefficient map. If all coefficients of $f$ vanish, then $f$ is orthogonal to the linear span of the basis. Completeness makes this span dense, and continuity of $g\mapsto\langle f,g\rangle$ gives $\langle f,f\rangle=0$, hence $f=0$ in $L^2$. Applying this to the difference of two functions proves injectivity. Thus the coefficient map is a continuous linear embedding $L^2([0,1])\hookrightarrow H(\delta)$.

The weight trace $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}$ is finite exactly when $\delta>1/2$: for wavelets its tail is a constant multiple of $\sum_{l\ge1}l^{-2\delta}$, while for a trigonometric basis it is comparable to $\sum_{l\ge2}[l(\log l)^{2\delta}]^{-1}$. The product-prior theorem below uses the wavelet case.

> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $p_0$ be a finite-valued probability density on $\mathbb R$
with compact support. Assume $p_0\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ and, with the
integrands set to zero on $\{p_0=0\}$,
$$\int_{\{p_0>0\}}\left[\left(\frac{p_0''}{p_0}\right)^2+
\left(\frac{p_0'}{p_0}\right)^4\right]p_0\,dx<\infty,$$
and assume there is $C<\infty$ such that
$$h(p_0,p_0*\phi_\sigma)\le C\sigma^2$$
for all sufficiently small $\sigma>0$. Here $h$ is the root-L2 Hellinger
distance of [[def-hellinger-distance-between-density-laws]], and
$\phi_\sigma$ is the centered normal density with standard deviation
$\sigma$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a finite nonzero
measure with a continuous, strictly positive Lebesgue density on an open
interval containing $\operatorname{supp}(p_0)$, and independently let
$S\sim G$ on $(0,\infty)$. For $\sigma=\sigma_nS$, define
$$p_{F,\sigma}(x)=\int\phi_\sigma(x-z)F(dz),$$
and observe $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ IID from $p_0$. Suppose
$$n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2},\qquad
0<a_2<a_1<1,\qquad a_2\ge(4+\gamma)^{-1},$$
and, for some $\beta>0$ and $\gamma>1$,
$$G((0,s])\lesssim e^{-\beta s^{-\gamma}}\ (s\downarrow0),\qquad
G((s,\infty))\lesssim e^{-\beta s^\gamma}\ (s\to\infty).$$
Here $u_n\lesssim v_n$ means $u_n\le Cv_n$ eventually for a fixed
constant $C$. For every fixed
$\eta>\gamma/[2(\gamma-1)]$, put
$$\epsilon_n=\max\left\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,
n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta},\ \sigma_n^2\log n\right\}.$$
Then for every sufficiently large fixed $M$,
$$\Pi_n\!\left(h(p_{F,\sigma},p_0)>M\epsilon_n\mid X_{1:n}\right)
\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability. If $G$ is compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$,
the middle term $n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta}$ may be omitted. The conclusion
is only in probability; it supplies no almost-sure contraction or generic
minimax-optimality assertion.

Assume AC. Let $p_0\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a probability density with compact support $K$, a finite union of intervals. Suppose $J=\int_{\{p_0>0\}}(p_0'')^2/p_0<\infty$ and there are $a,c>0$ such that $P_0(I)\ge c\lambda(I)^a$ for every interval $I\subseteq K$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a finite nonzero measure with continuous strictly positive density on a neighborhood of $K$, and independently let $S\sim G$ for any probability measure $G$ on $(0,\infty)$. Suppose $n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$ for $0<a_2<a_1<1$, and put $\sigma=\sigma_nS$. Then for constants $C_1,C_2>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
$$ \Pi_n\left\{\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{F,\sigma})\le C_1\sigma_n^4,\quad P_0\left[\log\frac{p_0}{p_{F,\sigma}}\right]^2\le C_1\sigma_n^4\right\}\ge\exp\{-C_2\sigma_n^{-1}(\log n)^2\}. $$
Consequently, for $d_n=\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,\sigma_n^2\}$, the same two local quantities are at most $C_1d_n^2$ on a set of prior mass at least $e^{-C_3nd_n^2}$. Logarithmic integrands vanish where $p_0=0$.

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ be a measurable parameter space, $\Pi$ a prior probability measure on it, and $p_\theta$ a jointly measurable family of finite-valued probability densities relative to one fixed sigma-finite measure $\mu$. Let $P_0$ have finite-valued density $p_0$ relative to $\mu$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID with law $P_0$. Assume the Axiom of Choice for the imported directional KL convention ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The jointly measurable density family is explicit input, so no arbitrary-index selection of versions is used here. In the expression below, the weighted log terms are set to zero on $\{p_0=0\}$; on $\{p_0>0,p_\theta=0\}$ the log ratio is $-\infty$ and its square is $+\infty$. For $\epsilon_n>0$, define
$$K_n:=\left\{\theta:\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_\theta)\le\epsilon_n^2,\quad \int\left[\log\frac{p_\theta}{p_0}\right]^2p_0\,d\mu\le\epsilon_n^2\right\}.$$
Joint measurability and Tonelli make $K_n$ measurable, as verified below. If $\Pi(K_n)\ge e^{-Cn\epsilon_n^2}$ for $C>0$ and $\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_\theta)$ uses the direction in [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]], then, defining the ratio to be zero on the $P_0$-null set where $p_0=0$, the likelihood denominator
$$D_n:=\int_\Theta\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{p_\theta(X_i)}{p_0(X_i)}\,\Pi(d\theta)$$
is finite and positive $P_0^n$-almost surely and
$$P_0^n\!\left\{D_n\ge e^{-(C+2)n\epsilon_n^2}\right\}\ge1-\frac1{n\epsilon_n^2}.$$

Assume AC. Let $p_0$ be supported on a compact interval $I=[L,U]$ with
$L<U$, let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$ for a finite nonzero base measure whose
density is bounded below on a neighborhood of $I$, and let $S\sim G$ be
independent with $\sigma=\sigma_nS$. Put $R=(U-L)/2$ and, for $d>0$,
$I_d=[L-d,U+d]$.
Observe IID data from $p_0$ under the location-mixture density
$p_{F,\sigma}$. Let $\epsilon_n,\delta_n>0$ with
$n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$ and $n\delta_n^2\to\infty$. Suppose the local KL
and log-square prior-mass condition gives a denominator event
$$P_0^n\{D_n\ge e^{-C_0n\delta_n^2}\}\longrightarrow1,$$
where $D_n=\int\prod_i p_{F,\sigma}(X_i)/p_0(X_i)\,\Pi_n(dF,d\sigma)$.
Choose $s_n\to0$ and put $q_n=2\Phi(-R/s_n)$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function. If
$$nq_n-(C_0+2)n\delta_n^2\to\infty,\qquad
n\epsilon_n^{-2}s_n^{-1}e^{-d^2/(2s_n^2)}\to0,$$
then the posterior complement of
$$\mathcal S_n:=\{(F,\sigma):\sigma\le s_n,\ F(I_d^c)\le\epsilon_n^2\}$$
converges to zero in $P_0^n$-probability.

Fix $A\ge1$ independently of $n$. The constants in the entropy estimates
and the required fixed $M_0$ may depend on $A$. Let $0<a_2<a_1<1$,
$n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$, and
$\gamma>1$. Suppose $G$ is a probability measure on $(0,\infty)$ satisfying
$G((0,s])\le C e^{-\beta s^{-\gamma}}$ for all sufficiently small $s>0$.
Let $s_n\to0$ with $s_n/\sigma_n\to\infty$. For integers $j$ with
$2^j\sigma_n\le s_n$, put $\widetilde r_n:=\min\{r_n,1/4\}$ and
$$\mathcal P_{n,j}:=\{p_{F,\sigma}:F([-A,A]^c)\le\widetilde r_n^2/8,
\quad 2^j\sigma_n\le\sigma<2^{j+1}\sigma_n,\quad \sigma\le s_n\},$$
and let $\pi_{n,j}$ be the prior mass of the corresponding parameter band,
so $\pi_{n,j}\le G([2^j,2^{j+1}))$. Suppose $r_n>0$ and, for some fixed
sufficiently large $M_0$ (allowed to depend on $A$) and fixed
$\eta>\gamma/[2(\gamma-1)]$,
$$r_n\ge M_0\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,
n^{-1/2}\sigma_n^{-\eta}\}.$$
With $N_{n,j}=N(r_n,\mathcal P_{n,j},h)$, one has
$$e^{-nr_n^2}\sum_{j:2^j\sigma_n\le s_n}\sqrt{N_{n,j}\pi_{n,j}}\longrightarrow0.$$
If instead $G$ is supported on a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$, the same
conclusion holds under the first rate term alone.

Assume AC. For each $n$, let $\Pi_n$ be a prior on a measurable parameter
space $\Theta_n^*$, and let $p_\theta$ be a jointly measurable family of finite-valued densities
against one sigma-finite measure, and let $p_0$ be the true density for IID
data $X_1,\ldots,X_n$. Let $\epsilon_n,\delta_n>0$ satisfy
$\delta_n\le\epsilon_n$, $n\delta_n^2\to\infty$, and
$n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$. Suppose for a constant $C_0>0$ that
$$\Pi_n\!\left\{\theta:\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_\theta)\le\delta_n^2,\quad
P_0\left[\log\frac{p_0}{p_\theta}\right]^2\le\delta_n^2\right\}\ge e^{-C_0n\delta_n^2}.$$
Let $S_n\subseteq\Theta_n^*$ be a measurable sieve with
$\Pi_n(S_n^c\mid X_{1:n})\to0$ in $P_0^n$-probability. Partition it into
countably many measurable sets $S_{n,j}$, put $\pi_{n,j}=\Pi_n(S_{n,j})$,
and let $N_{n,j}=N(\epsilon_n,\{p_\theta:\theta\in S_{n,j}\},h)$ be the
finite covering number as defined in [[def-covering-packing-bracketing-number-and-metric-entropy]], with centers in that density class, whenever $\pi_{n,j}>0$. If
$$e^{-n\epsilon_n^2}\sum_{j:\pi_{n,j}>0}\sqrt{N_{n,j}\pi_{n,j}}\longrightarrow0,$$
then for every sufficiently large fixed $M$, the posterior mass of
$$\{\theta:h(p_\theta,p_0)>M\epsilon_n\}$$
converges to zero in $P_0^n$-probability.

Let $\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$ be the probability measures on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$, equipped with the evaluation sigma-algebra, and let $\sigma>0$.
For $F\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$ define
$$p_{F,\sigma}(x):=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-z)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)F(dz).$$
Then $(F,\sigma,x)\mapsto p_{F,\sigma}(x)$ is jointly measurable,
$0<p_{F,\sigma}(x)\le(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})^{-1}$ for every $(F,\sigma,x)$,
and $\int_{\mathbb R}p_{F,\sigma}(x)\,dx=1$. In particular it is the
Lebesgue density of the convolution of $F$ with $N(0,\sigma^2)$.

derivations.claim: The $C^2$ compact truth in [F1] satisfies the $J$ hypothesis of [F2] by the stated derivative integrability condition. All other hypotheses of [F2] are either in [F1] or the interval-mass premise. Choose a fixed $C\ge1$ large enough that, with $\bar d_n=\sqrt C d_n$, the local set has both quantities at most $\bar d_n^2$ and mass at least $e^{-n\bar d_n^2}$. By [F3], its denominator is at least $e^{-3n\bar d_n^2}$ with probability tending to one, since $n\bar d_n^2\ge C\sigma_n^{-1}(\log n)^2\to\infty$.

Let $\epsilon_n$ denote the displayed improved rate, omitting its middle term if $G$ is compactly supported. Put $r_n=M_0\epsilon_n$ for a sufficiently large fixed $M_0$ and $\xi_n=\min\{r_n,1/4\}/\sqrt8$. Then $\bar d_n\le r_n$ after increasing $M_0$, $n\xi_n^2\to\infty$ and $\xi_n^{-2}\le C'n$: use $\epsilon_n\ge(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n\ge n^{-1/2}\log n$ eventually when $r_n<1/4$, while otherwise $\xi_n$ is fixed. Choose a compact interval $I=[L,U]$ containing the truth support in its interior, within the interval on which the base density is positive. Put $R=(U-L)/2>0$ and $\kappa=\max\{a_1,1-4a_2,0\}<1$. The bandwidth bounds give $n\bar d_n^2\le C'n^\kappa(\log n)^2$. Choose $s_n=c_0(\log n)^{-1/2}$ with $c_0$ large enough that $q_n=2\Phi(-R/s_n)\ge n^{-\theta}$ eventually for some $0<\theta<1-\kappa$. This follows by integrating the standard normal density over $[R/s_n,R/s_n+1]$ once $R^2/(2c_0^2)<\theta$. Thus $nq_n-5n\bar d_n^2\to\infty$.

Choose $d>0$ with $d^2/(2c_0^2)>4$ and a fixed $A\ge1$ large enough that $I_d=[L-d,U+d]\subseteq[-A,A]$. Then $n\xi_n^{-2}s_n^{-1}e^{-d^2/(2s_n^2)}\to0$, by the inverse-radius bound in step 1.2. With denominator coefficient $3$, all hypotheses of [F4] hold at local radius $\bar d_n$ and location-tail tolerance $\xi_n$. It follows that the posterior complement of $S_n=\{\sigma\le s_n,F([-A,A]^c)\le\xi_n^2\}$ vanishes in sampling probability: [F4] first gives the smaller location sieve using $I_d$, and $[-A,A]^c\subseteq I_d^c$.

Partition $S_n$ into the measurable dyadic scale bands $S_{n,j}=S_n\cap\{2^j\sigma_n\le\sigma<2^{j+1}\sigma_n\}$. Their prior masses are bounded by $G([2^j,2^{j+1}))$. We have $s_n/\sigma_n\to\infty$, and $\xi_n^2=\min\{r_n,1/4\}^2/8$ matches the tail tolerance in [F5]. Thus [F5] supplies $e^{-nr_n^2}\sum_j\sqrt{N(r_n,\{p_{F,\sigma}:(F,\sigma)\in S_{n,j}\},h)\Pi_n(S_{n,j})}\to0$. For compactly supported $G$, its compact branch applies with the first term alone. The preceding steps used only $d_n$ and the retained first term, so they also apply unchanged to this improved compact-scale rate.

By [F7] the model has the jointly measurable density likelihood required in [F6]. Step 1.1 gives the local mass condition, step 1.3 gives the sieve complement, and step 2.1 gives the weighted entropy condition at target radius $r_n$. Both $n\bar d_n^2$ and $nr_n^2$ diverge, and $\bar d_n\le r_n$. Apply [F6] to obtain posterior contraction at every sufficiently large fixed multiple of $r_n=M_0\epsilon_n$, in $P_0^n$-probability. Absorbing $M_0$ into the final constant proves the Statement, including its compact-scale branch.

boundaries.reason: The object is a probability density and hence is not empty; no empty finite-family assertion occurs.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and proof set logarithmic integrands to zero where the truth density vanishes; all smoothing and mixture densities have positive scale.

boundaries.reason: There is no unit-probability endpoint assertion; credibility lies strictly between zero and one.

boundaries.evidence: Statement assumes a probability density, positive scale, finite nonzero base measure and fixed positive-mass compact scale event where used; the identically zero density is excluded.
Statement assumes positive Gaussian scale and compact truth support; proof handles support endpoints, kernel limits at zero and the compact-scale prior branch where relevant.
Statement inherits AC from the normal, KL and Dirichlet-process suppliers; all extra choices are finite partitions or finite approximations and a fixed positive-mass scale interval.

Choose a fixed $C\ge1$ large enough that, with $\bar d_n=\sqrt C d_n$, the local set has both quantities at most $\bar d_n^2$ and mass at least $e^{-n\bar d_n^2}$. By [F3], its denominator is at least $e^{-3n\bar d_n^2}$ with probability tending to one, since $n\bar d_n^2\ge C\sigma_n^{-1}(\log n)^2\to\infty$.

Let $\epsilon_n$ denote the displayed improved rate, omitting its middle term if $G$ is compactly supported. Put $r_n=M_0\epsilon_n$ for a sufficiently large fixed $M_0$ and $\xi_n=\min\{r_n,1/4\}/\sqrt8$. Then $\bar d_n\le r_n$ after increasing $M_0$, $n\xi_n^2\to\infty$ and $\xi_n^{-2}\le C'n$: use $\epsilon_n\ge(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n\ge n^{-1/2}\log n$ eventually when $r_n<1/4$, while otherwise $\xi_n$ is fixed. Choose a compact interval $I=[L,U]$ containing the truth support in its interior, within the interval on which the base density is positive. Put $R=(U-L)/2>0$ and $\kappa=\max\{a_1,1-4a_2,0\}<1$. The bandwidth bounds give $n\bar d_n^2\le C'n^\kappa(\log n)^2$. Choose $s_n=c_0(\log n)^{-1/2}$ with $c_0$ large enough that $q_n=2\Phi(-R/s_n)\ge n^{-\theta}$ eventually for some $0<\theta<1-\kappa$. This follows by integrating the standard normal density over $[R/s_n,R/s_n+1]$ once $R^2/(2c_0^2)<\theta$. Thus $nq_n-5n\bar d_n^2\to\infty$.

Choose $d>0$ with $d^2/(2c_0^2)>4$ and a fixed $A\ge1$ large enough that $I_d=[L-d,U+d]\subseteq[-A,A]$. Then $n\xi_n^{-2}s_n^{-1}e^{-d^2/(2s_n^2)}\to0$, by the inverse-radius bound in step 1.2. With denominator coefficient $3$, all hypotheses of [F4] hold at local radius $\bar d_n$ and location-tail tolerance $\xi_n$. It follows that the posterior complement of $S_n=\{\sigma\le s_n,F([-A,A]^c)\le\xi_n^2\}$ vanishes in sampling probability: [F4] first gives the smaller location sieve using $I_d$, and $[-A,A]^c\subseteq I_d^c$.

Partition $S_n$ into the measurable dyadic scale bands $S_{n,j}=S_n\cap\{2^j\sigma_n\le\sigma<2^{j+1}\sigma_n\}$. Their prior masses are bounded by $G([2^j,2^{j+1}))$. We have $s_n/\sigma_n\to\infty$, and $\xi_n^2=\min\{r_n,1/4\}^2/8$ matches the tail tolerance in [F5]. Thus [F5] supplies $e^{-nr_n^2}\sum_j\sqrt{N(r_n,\{p_{F,\sigma}:(F,\sigma)\in S_{n,j}\},h)\Pi_n(S_{n,j})}\to0$. For compactly supported $G$, its compact branch applies with the first term alone. The preceding steps used only $d_n$ and the retained first term, so they also apply unchanged to this improved compact-scale rate.

By [F7] the model has the jointly measurable density likelihood required in [F6]. Step 1.1 gives the local mass condition, step 1.3 gives the sieve complement, and step 2.1 gives the weighted entropy condition at target radius $r_n$. Both $n\bar d_n^2$ and $nr_n^2$ diverge, and $\bar d_n\le r_n$. Apply [F6] to obtain posterior contraction at every sufficiently large fixed multiple of $r_n=M_0\epsilon_n$, in $P_0^n$-probability. Absorbing $M_0$ into the final constant proves the Statement, including its compact-scale branch.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID on $[0,1]$ with density $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, and suppose $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$. Use a sufficiently regular compactly supported boundary corrected orthonormal multiresolution wavelet basis satisfying [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], with regularity greater than $\alpha$, and let $V_L$ contain exactly its wavelet levels through $L$, including the fixed low scaling space and constants. Its regularity and vanishing moments satisfy the composition hypotheses in that lemma for some integer $m>\alpha$. Let $L_n$ be either of the two cutoff sequences in [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], fixed consistently for all $n$.

In Type-S1 take $\alpha>1$, $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, and any coefficient probability density with globally Lipschitz logarithm. In Type-S2 take $\alpha>1/2$, Gaussian coefficients, and $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$ with $0<r<\alpha-1/4$. Normalize $f=\exp(T)/\int\exp(T)$ as in that definition. For every admissible weight sequence $w$, the posterior satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}\bigl(\mathcal L(\sqrt n(f-P_n(L_n))\mid X^n),\mathcal L(G_{P_0})\bigr)\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where $P_n(L_n)$ has empirical wavelet coefficients through $L_n$ and zero coefficients above $L_n$, and $G_{P_0}$ is the Borel Gaussian bridge with covariance $P_0[(\psi_i-P_0\psi_i)(\psi_j-P_0\psi_j)]$.

Assume AC. Use the type-H prior of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], retaining its original conditions: $1/2<\alpha\le1$, $f_0\in C^\alpha([0,1])$, $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, either original cutoff $L_n=j_n$ or $L_n=\ell_n$, and $c_1 2^{-L_na}\le a_{k,L_n}\le c_2$ for fixed positive $a,c_1,c_2$. Write $m_n=2^{L_n}$. In the Haar convention, the scaling function is $1$, the detail functions are
$$\psi_{lk}=2^{l/2}(\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k}}-\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k+1}}),\qquad l\ge0,\quad 0\le k<2^l,$$
and a histogram at resolution $L_n$ has only the scaling coordinate and levels $l<L_n$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID from $f_0$, let $N_{nk}=\sum_i\mathbf1_{I_{L_n,k}}(X_i)$, and define the empirical histogram
$$h_n(x)=m_n N_{nk}/n\quad\text{on }I_{L_n,k}.$$
Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$ be the density posterior for the stated histogram prior. For every nondecreasing $w_l\ge1$ with $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, its conditional law $Q_n$ of $\sqrt n(f-h_n)$ satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}(Q_n,\mathcal L(G_{P_0}))\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where the Borel centered Gaussian bridge $G_{P_0}$ is supplied by [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]] and has covariance $P_0[(\psi-P_0\psi)(\psi'-P_0\psi')]$. Its scaling coordinate is zero. This proves the type-H source-specific posterior BvM with the empirical projection center; no additional contraction, bias, or Dirichlet-parameter condition is imposed.

Let $V_L$ be the span of wavelets through level $L$ in a compactly supported orthonormal multiresolution basis on $[0,1]$, either boundary corrected or periodized. Assume constants belong to $V_L$, its dimension $d_L\asymp2^L$, and its orthonormal scaling functions $\phi_{Lk}$ have supremum norm at most $C2^{L/2}$, support diameter at most $C2^{-L}$, and uniformly bounded overlap. Periodized supports and distances are interpreted on the circle. Assume also $\sum_k|\psi_{lk}(x)|\le C2^{l/2}$ and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_1\le C2^{-l/2}$. Let $P_L$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $V_L$.

Then $P_L$ has a kernel $K_L$ satisfying $\sup_x\int|K_L(x,y)|dy\le C'$ and $K_L(x,y)=0$ when $\operatorname{dist}(x,y)>C'2^{-L}$. If $a$ is $\beta$-Hölder for $0<\beta\le1$, then
$$\|P_L(ah)-ah\|_\infty\le C'\|a\|_{C^\beta}2^{-\beta L}\|h\|_\infty,\qquad h\in V_L.$$
For the composition assertion, assume additionally an integer $m>\alpha$ such that $\|\psi_{lk}^{(q)}\|_\infty\le C_q2^{l(q+1/2)}$ for $0\le q\le m$, bounded overlap also for their derivatives, and vanishing moments through degree $m-1$ for the detail wavelets, including boundary wavelets; the finite low scaling functions are $C^m$. These are the usual sufficiently regular compact wavelet hypotheses. If a bounded function $g$ has coefficients bounded by $C_g2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, with $\alpha>0$, and its wavelet expansion represents $g$ in $L^2$, then $\|g-P_Lg\|_\infty\le C''C_g2^{-\alpha L}$, up to equality of the continuous representatives. Under these additional derivative and cancellation hypotheses, $e^g$ also has coefficients bounded by $C_g^\prime2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, including integer $\alpha$, and $g,e^g$ are $\beta$-Hölder for every $0<\beta<\min(\alpha,1)$. Moreover $\|h\|_\infty\le C''\sqrt{d_L}\|h\|_2$ for $h\in V_L$.

Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have a density $f_0$ on $[0,1]$ with $\|f_0\|_\infty\le B<\infty$. Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be an orthonormal, compactly supported wavelet basis with $2^l$ coefficients at level $l\ge1$, uniformly bounded overlap, and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_\infty\le C_0 2^{l/2}$. Suppose for some $\gamma>1/2$,
$$\max_k|\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle|\le C_f2^{-l(\gamma+1/2)}.$$
Let $w_l\ge1$ be nondecreasing and admissible in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], and choose either cutoff regime
$$2^{L_n}\asymp n^{1/(2\gamma+1)}\quad\text{or}\quad 2^{L_n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\gamma+1)}.$$
For IID $X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim P_0$, define the finite wavelet projection $P_n(L_n)$ by coefficients $\langle P_n(L_n),\psi_{lk}\rangle=P_n\psi_{lk}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{lk}(X_i)$ for $l\le L_n$ and zero for $l>L_n$, with the coarsest scaling coordinates projected as well. Let $G_{P_0}$ be a Borel centered Gaussian law on $M_0(w)$ whose coefficient covariance is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(G_{lk},G_{l'k'})=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Then
$$\sqrt n\{P_n(L_n)-f_0\}\Rightarrow G_{P_0}\quad\text{in }M_0(w).$$

Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have density $0<\rho\le f_0\le D<\infty$ on $[0,1]$, and put $F_0(t)=\int_0^t f_0$. Use a complete real orthonormal wavelet basis, allowing the Haar basis with its finite scaling coordinate, and admissible weights $w$ as in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]]. Assume the wavelet geometry and summability conditions of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]], and write $J:M_0(w)\to C([0,1])$ for its primitive map. Let $G$ be the Borel centered Gaussian bridge random element of [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]], with coefficient covariance
$$\operatorname{Cov}(G_{lk},G_{l'k'})=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Then the distribution functions of $\|G\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|JG\|_\infty$ are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$. Both assign probability zero to $0$, and take values strictly between $0$ and $1$ at every positive argument. Consequently, for every $u\in(0,1)$, each has a unique positive finite lower $u$-quantile $q$, with CDF value $u$, and is strictly increasing on an open neighborhood of $q$.

Let $P_0$ have a density $f_0$ on $[0,1]$ bounded above and bounded away from zero, and put $F_0(t)=\int_0^t f_0(x)dx$. Use the wavelet basis and $M_0(w)$ of [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], and assume the wavelet conditions and summability condition $\sum_lw_l2^{-l/2}<\infty$ of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]]. Let $T_n$ be a measurable $L^2$-valued center, let $\Pi_n$ be a posterior kernel supported on $L^2$ densities, and define $Q_n$ to be the conditional law on $M_0(w)$ of $\sqrt n(f-T_n)$ under $f\sim\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$.

Assume under $P_0^n$ that (i) $Q_n$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance in probability to the centered Gaussian bridge coefficient law $G_{P_0}$ in $M_0(w)$, whose finite coefficient covariances are $P_0[(h-P_0h)(g-P_0g)]$, and (ii) $\sqrt n(T_n-f_0)\Rightarrow G_{P_0}$ in $M_0(w)$. For $u=1-\alpha$, let $q_M$ and $q_C$ be the lower $u$-quantiles of $\|G_{P_0}\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|JG_{P_0}\|_\infty$. Assume both CDFs are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on open neighborhoods of their respective quantiles, and that $q_M,q_C>0$. These local quantile conditions allow the CDFs to be constant on the negative half-line. In the projected empirical-center case $T_n=P_n(L_n)$, [[thm-projected-empirical-process-clt-in-m0w]] supplies premise (ii) under its stated smoothness and cutoff conditions. For the source-specific type-S and type-H priors, the posterior BvM premise (i) is established in [[thm-type-s-density-weak-bvm-on-m0w]] and [[thm-type-h-histogram-posterior-weak-bvm-in-m0w]], respectively.

For a posterior draw $f$, write $F_f=Jf$ and $F_{T_n}=JT_n$, where $J$ is the primitive map of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]]. Then the posterior law of $\sqrt n(F_f-F_{T_n})$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance on $C([0,1])$ to the $P_0$-Brownian bridge $B_{P_0}(t)$, with covariance $F_0(s\wedge t)-F_0(s)F_0(t)$.

For $0<\alpha<1$, let $R_n^M$ and $R_n^C$ be the posterior lower $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\|\sqrt n(f-T_n)\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|\sqrt n(F_f-F_{T_n})\|_\infty$, respectively. The corresponding posterior balls
$$C_n^M=\{f:\|f-T_n\|_{M(w)}\le R_n^M/\sqrt n\},\qquad C_n^C=\{F:\|F-F_{T_n}\|_\infty\le R_n^C/\sqrt n\}$$
are measurable credible sets of posterior mass at least $1-\alpha$. Their frequentist coverage tends to $1-\alpha$, and the scaled radii converge to the respective $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\|G_{P_0}\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|B_{P_0}\|_\infty$.

Use the $M_0(w)$ credible ball $C_n^M$ and radius $R_n^M$ of [[thm-cdf-and-multiscale-credible-band-calibration-from-bvm]]. Let $\gamma>0$, assume the compactly supported wavelets have uniformly bounded overlap and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_\infty\le C2^{l/2}$, and define
$$\|f\|_{C^\gamma_\psi}:=\sup_{l,k}2^{l(\gamma+1/2)}|\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle|.$$
Suppose $\|f_0\|_{C^\gamma_\psi}<\infty$. Choose integers $j_n$ with $2^{j_n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\gamma+1)}$ and let $u_n=w_{j_n}/\sqrt{j_n}\to\infty$. Intersect the credible ball with the coefficient smoothness ball:
$$\overline C_n=C_n^M\cap\{f:\|f\|_{C^\gamma_\psi}\le u_n\}.$$
Then $P_{f_0}^{(n)}\{f_0\in\overline C_n\}\to1-\alpha$, and its $L^\infty$ diameter satisfies
$$\operatorname{diam}_{L^\infty}(\overline C_n)=O_{P_{f_0}^{(n)}}\!\left((n/\log n)^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}u_n\right).$$

derivations.claim: In Type S, [F1] proves posterior BvM about $T_n=P_n(L_n)$ with the original S1 range $\alpha>1$ and original Gaussian S2 range $\alpha>1/2$, $0<r<\alpha-1/4$. The truth $g_0=\log f_0$ has $\alpha$ coefficient regularity, so [F2] gives that regularity for $f_0=e^{g_0}$ as well. The retained basis has the support, overlap and supremum bounds required by the empirical-process theorem in [F2]. Taking $\gamma=\alpha>1/2$ and the given cutoff therefore proves its sampling-center CLT with the same Gaussian bridge.

In Type H, [F1] proves posterior BvM about the empirical histogram $h_n$. Haar wavelets have the same support, overlap and supremum bounds. The ordinary $\alpha$-Hölder truth, $1/2<\alpha\le1$, has Haar coefficients bounded by $C2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$: subtract its value at one point of the support in the coefficient integral, use the zero mean, support diameter $2^{-l}$ and $L^1$ norm $2^{-l/2}$. The histogram projection retains details through $J_n=L_n-1$. Both given cutoff regimes remain true with this $J_n$, since multiplying $2^{L_n}$ by $1/2$ changes only their comparison constants. Thus [F2] with $\gamma=\alpha$ gives the sampling CLT about this exact histogram center. The finite scaling coordinate is included and its centered fluctuation is zero.

In all three cases, positivity and boundedness of $f_0$, admissibility, and the displayed summability verify [F3]. Hence every norm-quantile assumption of [F4] holds at $u=1-\eta$. Steps 1.1–1.2 verify its posterior and sampling premises, with the same coefficient covariance law. Applying [F4] proves all asserted CDF limits, measurable credibility, radius limits and frequentist coverage, for the exact empirical centers and every $0<\eta<1$.

When the additional hypotheses in the last paragraph of the Statement hold, the multiscale credible ball just obtained is precisely the input to [F5]. Applying that theorem yields its smoothness-intersection coverage and stated diameter rate. These are additional hypotheses only for this diameter conclusion; the coverage and CDF conclusions in step 2.1 required no such extra conditions.

boundaries.reason: The sampling truth is a probability density on [0,1], so the model is nonempty.

boundaries.evidence: The bridge norm quantile supplier proves strictly positive finite interior radii; the deterministic scaling coordinate is allowed to be zero.
The uniform density example verifies all premises and both specific prior constructions.
Credibility level has 0<eta<1; smoothness/range/cutoff endpoints remain exactly the cited supplier hypotheses.
Full AC is explicit and inherited from the density bridge, posterior BvM and finite sampling CLT suppliers.

before_contract.finite_check_disposition: No finite smoke obligation; this is a direct application of the fully proved local suppliers.
before_contract.claim:
Assume AC. Use either Type-S1, Type-S2 or Type-H with all the truth, basis, prior-scale, Dirichlet-parameter and cutoff conditions of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]]. Let $w_l\ge1$ be nondecreasing, $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, and $\sum_lw_l2^{-l/2}<\infty$. In Type S take $T_n=P_n(L_n)$, the empirical wavelet projection through level $L_n$. In Type H take the empirical histogram $T_n=h_n$ at mesh $2^{-L_n}$, equivalently the Haar projection with scaling coordinate and details $l<L_n$.

For each $0<\eta<1$, the posterior multiscale and CDF balls of [[thm-cdf-and-multiscale-credible-band-calibration-from-bvm]], at posterior level $1-\eta$ and centered at these $T_n$, have posterior mass at least $1-\eta$ and frequentist coverage tending to $1-\eta$. Their scaled radii converge in probability to the positive finite $1-\eta$ quantiles of the corresponding Gaussian bridge norms. In particular the CDF posterior converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance to the $P_0$-Brownian bridge law.

If additionally the coefficient smoothness and undersmoothing hypotheses of [[thm-multiscale-credible-band-holder-diameter]] hold, its intersection with the stated coefficient smoothness ball has the same limiting coverage and the diameter bound asserted there. No unverified entropy, prior-mass, posterior contraction or quantile-regularity premise is required in this corollary.

Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the S-regular wavelet basis in [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]], with $2^l$ coefficients at each level $l\ge0$. For $\alpha>0$, put $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and let the prior on $f=\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ have IID coefficients $\xi_{lk}$ with density $\varphi$. Assume countable choice for the $L^2$ prior construction supplied by [[lem-wavelet-product-prior-is-l2-valued]], and take the full posterior kernel as the supplied model input of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $f_0\in L^2([0,1])$, write $\theta_{0,lk}=\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle$ and $r_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}/\sigma_l$, and suppose

$$\sup_{l,k}|r_{lk}|\le M<\tau,$$

where $\varphi$ is a probability density satisfying $\varphi(u)\le C_\varphi$ for every $u$, $\varphi(u)\ge c_\varphi>0$ for $|u|<\tau$, $\int u^2\varphi(u)\,du<\infty$, and $\varphi$ is continuous at each $r_{lk}$. The observation model is

$$dX^{(n)}(t)=f_0(t)\,dt+n^{-1/2}dW(t),\qquad 0\le t\le1,$$

with standard white noise $W$; in the stated basis this is the sequence experiment $X_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}+n^{-1/2}Z_{lk}$ with independent standard normal coordinates. Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)$ be the product-coordinate posterior of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $N$ be the law of the canonical white noise in $H(\delta)$ and define

$$\widetilde\Pi_n:=\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)\circ[f\mapsto\sqrt n(f-X)]^{-1},\qquad \beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\mu,\nu):=\sup_{\substack{\|g\|_\infty\le1\\ \operatorname{Lip}_{H(\delta)}(g)\le1}}\left|\int g\,d\mu-\int g\,d\nu\right|.$$

For every $\delta>1/2$,

$$\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,N)\longrightarrow0$$

in probability under the true white-noise law $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$. This is a bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM conclusion; it asserts neither total-variation convergence on all Borel subsets nor an $L^2$-valued Gaussian limit.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(S,d)$ be a Polish space, and let $\mu_n,\mu$ be Borel probability measures on $S$. Define

$$\beta_{BL}(\nu,\rho):=\sup\left\{\left|\int g\,d\nu-\int g\,d\rho\right|:g:S\to\mathbb R,\ \|g\|_\infty\le1,\ \operatorname{Lip}_d(g)\le1\right\},$$

where $\operatorname{Lip}_d(g):=\sup_{x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/d(x,y)$, with value $0$ when $S$ has at most one point. Then

$$\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\beta_{BL}(\mu_n,\mu)\longrightarrow0,$$

where $\Rightarrow$ is weak convergence of Borel probabilities ([[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]). The implication from bounded-Lipschitz convergence to weak convergence is choice-free; the reverse implication below uses AC through Prokhorov's theorem.

For Borel probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on a metric space S, write $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ if $\int f\,d\mu_n\to\int f\,d\mu$ for every bounded continuous real function f on S. Continuity is [[def-metric-continuity]]. Such f is Borel measurable (inverse images of open sets are open) and $\int|f|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\mu(S)<\infty$, so the integrals are finite in [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. No completeness or coupling is required.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

before_contract.claim:
Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a countable complete orthonormal basis of the real Hilbert space $L^2([0,1])$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). For a wavelet basis, index levels by $l\ge0$, let $K_l$ have $2^l$ indices, and put $a_l=2^l$ for $l\ge1$ and $a_0=2$ for the finite coarsest level. This finite-level convention only prevents a zero logarithmic weight and does not change any convergence criterion below. For a trigonometric basis, use its integer frequency index $l$, bounded multiplicities, and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$.

Here an **$S$-regular wavelet basis** means a wavelet orthonormal basis whose members are $S$ times differentiable, with each derivative through order $S$ in $L^2([0,1])$, following the source convention. The weak BvM theorem below only uses the basis's completeness, orthonormality, and level counts.

For $\delta>0$, define $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ to be the space of coefficient sequences $c=(c_{lk})$ with norm

$$\|c\|_{H(\delta)}^2:=\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}|c_{lk}|^2<\infty.$$

Its inner product is the corresponding weighted coefficient inner product. Multiplying each coordinate by $a_l^{-1/2}(\log a_l)^{-\delta}$ identifies it isometrically with $\ell^2(I)$, where $I=\{(l,k):k\in K_l\}$ (or the corresponding trigonometric index set). This sequence space is complete: if $x^{(m)}$ is Cauchy, each coordinate converges to a scalar $x_i$; for every finite $F\subset I$, the Cauchy bound passes to the limit in $\sum_{i\in F}|x_i^{(m)}-x_i^{(n)}|^2$, so the supremum over finite $F$ shows $x^{(m)}\to x$ in $\ell^2(I)$. It is separable because finite-support sequences with rational coordinates form a countable dense set. Thus $H(\delta)$ is a separable Hilbert space without an additional choice assumption.

A function $f\in L^2([0,1])$ is identified with its coefficient sequence $c_{lk}=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$. For each finite set $F$ of indices, orthonormality makes $\sum_{(l,k)\in F}c_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ orthogonal to its residual in $L^2$, so the Pythagorean identity gives $\sum_F|c_{lk}|^2\le\|f\|_2^2$. Taking the supremum over finite $F$ and using the boundedness of the weights proves continuity of the coefficient map. If all coefficients of $f$ vanish, then $f$ is orthogonal to the linear span of the basis. Completeness makes this span dense, and continuity of $g\mapsto\langle f,g\rangle$ gives $\langle f,f\rangle=0$, hence $f=0$ in $L^2$. Applying this to the difference of two functions proves injectivity. Thus the coefficient map is a continuous linear embedding $L^2([0,1])\hookrightarrow H(\delta)$.

The weight trace $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}$ is finite exactly when $\delta>1/2$: for wavelets its tail is a constant multiple of $\sum_{l\ge1}l^{-2\delta}$, while for a trigonometric basis it is comparable to $\sum_{l\ge2}[l(\log l)^{2\delta}]^{-1}$. The product-prior theorem below uses the wavelet case.

before_contract.claim:
For type S use a fixed sufficiently regular compactly supported orthonormal multiresolution wavelet basis $(\psi_{lk})$ on $[0,1]$ as in [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]], with boundary correction, regularity greater than the truth smoothness $\alpha$, and $|K_l|=2^l$. The spaces $V_L$ spanned by the retained levels $l\le L$ contain constants and have orthonormal scaling bases with uniformly bounded overlap, support diameters at most $C2^{-L}$, and suprema at most $C2^{L/2}$; a fixed shift of the scaling-resolution index is absorbed in $C$. The wavelets likewise have uniformly bounded overlap, support diameters at most $C2^{-l}$, and suprema at most $C2^{l/2}$. For an integer $m>\alpha$, the detail wavelets have vanishing moments through degree $m-1$, and derivatives through order $m$ satisfy $\|\psi_{lk}^{(q)}\|_\infty\le C_q2^{l(q+1/2)}$, with uniformly bounded overlap of their supports; the fixed low scaling functions are $C^m$. These are the sufficiently regular compact multiresolution basis conditions in the source density theorem. For the density-model source results, every truth $f_0$ is a probability density satisfying $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$ for constants $\rho_0,D_0$. For $n\ge3$ and smoothness index $\alpha>0$, let $j_n$ and $\ell_n$ be the largest integers satisfying
$$2^{j_n}\le n^{1/(2\alpha+1)},\qquad 2^{\ell_n}\le(n/\log n)^{1/(2\alpha+1)}.$$
Choose one cutoff sequence $L_n\in\{j_n,\ell_n\}$ for all $n\ge3$; set any finite $L_n$ for $n=1,2$, which does not change asymptotic claims.

For a finite wavelet series $T_n=\sum_{l\le L_n}\sum_{k\in K_l}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}$, define $c(T_n)=\log\int_0^1e^{T_n(x)}dx$ and the normalized log-density $f_n(x)=e^{T_n(x)-c(T_n)}$.

The **type-S1 family** takes IID coefficients $\xi_{lk}$ with a continuous density $\varphi_H$ for which $\log\varphi_H$ is Lipschitz, and uses $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$. Its source theorem assumes $\log f_0$ has coefficient Hölder regularity $\alpha>1$ and $f_0$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero.

The **type-S2 family** takes IID standard-normal coefficients and uses $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$, where $0<r<\alpha-1/4$; its source theorem uses $\log f_0\in C^\alpha$, $\alpha>1/2$, and positive finite density bounds.

For the **type-H family**, use the Haar basis instead of the regular type-S wavelets: its scaling function is $1$ and $\psi_{lk}=2^{l/2}(1_{I_{l+1,2k}}-1_{I_{l+1,2k+1}})$ for $l\ge0$ and $0\le k<2^l$. The histogram space at resolution $L$ consists of the scaling coordinate and detail levels $l<L$; all detail coefficients at $l\ge L$ vanish. Partition $[0,1]$ into dyadic cells $I_{L_n,k}$ of length $2^{-L_n}$, draw $\omega=(\omega_k)_{k<2^{L_n}}\sim\operatorname{Dirichlet}(a_{0,L_n},\ldots,a_{2^{L_n}-1,L_n})$, and set $f_n=2^{L_n}\omega_k$ on cell $I_{L_n,k}$. The source assumptions are $c_1 2^{-L_na}\le a_{k,L_n}\le c_2$ for fixed positive $a,c_1,c_2$, and $f_0\in C^\alpha$ for $1/2<\alpha\le1$, together with the common positive finite density bounds above. The posterior asymptotic conclusions for these families are separate results.

Here $C^\alpha_\psi$ denotes the coefficient class with norm $\|g\|_{C^\alpha_\psi}:=\sup_{l,k}2^{l(\alpha+1/2)}|\langle g,\psi_{lk}\rangle|$. For sufficiently regular standard wavelets this is the usual Hölder scale (with the usual Zygmund interpretation at integer smoothness).

$$\int_{\{p_0>0\}}\left[\left(\frac{p_0''}{p_0}\right)^2+
\left(\frac{p_0'}{p_0}\right)^4\right]p_0\,dx<\infty,$$
and assume there is $C<\infty$ such that
$$h(p_0,p_0*\phi_\sigma)\le C\sigma^2$$
for all sufficiently small $\sigma>0$. Here $h$ is the root-L2 Hellinger
distance of [[def-hellinger-distance-between-density-laws]], and
$\phi_\sigma$ is the centered normal density with standard deviation
$\sigma$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a finite nonzero
measure with a continuous, strictly positive Lebesgue density on an open
interval containing $\operatorname{supp}(p_0)$, and independently let
$S\sim G$ on $(0,\infty)$. For $\sigma=\sigma_nS$, define
$$p_{F,\sigma}(x)=\int\phi_\sigma(x-z)F(dz),$$

$$n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2},\qquad
0<a_2<a_1<1,\qquad a_2\ge(4+\gamma)^{-1},$$
and, for some $\beta>0$ and $\gamma>1$,
$$G((0,s])\lesssim e^{-\beta s^{-\gamma}}\ (s\downarrow0),\qquad
G((s,\infty))\lesssim e^{-\beta s^\gamma}\ (s\to\infty).$$

constant $C$. For every fixed

$$\epsilon_n=\max\left\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,

Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space with a countable orthonormal basis $(\psi_{lk})$, where $K_l$ is the level-$l$ index set and $|K_l|=2^l$ for each $l\ge0$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). Such an $H$ is separable because finite rational linear combinations of the countable basis are dense. Let $\xi_{lk}$ be IID real random variables with common density $\varphi$ and finite second moment $m_2=\int x^2\varphi(x)\,dx<\infty$ ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]). For $\alpha>0$, set $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and form the partial wavelet sums

$$f_N=\sum_{0\le l\le N}\sum_{k\in K_l}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}.$$

Assume countable choice, denoted $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, when specializing to $H=L^2([0,1])$. Then $f_N$ converges almost surely in $H$ to a Borel $H$-valued random element $f$, and

$$\mathbb E\|f\|_H^2=m_2\sum_{l\ge0}2^l\sigma_l^2=m_2\sum_{l\ge0}2^{-2\alpha l}<\infty.$$

The abstract Hilbert-space assertion is choice-free; for $H=L^2([0,1])$, completeness follows from the Riesz–Fischer theorem under countable choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]]). More generally, finitely many additional coarsest orthogonal coordinates with fixed scales and finite coefficient second moments may be added; they contribute only a finite expectation to the displayed sum.

Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the S-regular wavelet basis in [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]], with $2^l$ coefficients at each level $l\ge0$. For $\alpha>0$, put $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and let the prior on $f=\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ have IID coefficients $\xi_{lk}$ with density $\varphi$. Assume countable choice for the $L^2$ prior construction supplied by [[lem-wavelet-product-prior-is-l2-valued]], and take the full posterior kernel as the supplied model input of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $f_0\in L^2([0,1])$, write $\theta_{0,lk}=\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle$ and $r_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}/\sigma_l$, and suppose

$$\sup_{l,k}|r_{lk}|\le M<\tau,$$

where $\varphi$ is a probability density satisfying $\varphi(u)\le C_\varphi$ for every $u$, $\varphi(u)\ge c_\varphi>0$ for $|u|<\tau$, $\int u^2\varphi(u)\,du<\infty$, and $\varphi$ is continuous at each $r_{lk}$. The observation model is

$$dX^{(n)}(t)=f_0(t)\,dt+n^{-1/2}dW(t),\qquad 0\le t\le1,$$

with standard white noise $W$; in the stated basis this is the sequence experiment $X_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}+n^{-1/2}Z_{lk}$ with independent standard normal coordinates. Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)$ be the product-coordinate posterior of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $N$ be the law of the canonical white noise in $H(\delta)$ and define

$$\widetilde\Pi_n:=\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)\circ[f\mapsto\sqrt n(f-X)]^{-1},\qquad \beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\mu,\nu):=\sup_{\substack{\|g\|_\infty\le1\\ \operatorname{Lip}_{H(\delta)}(g)\le1}}\left|\int g\,d\mu-\int g\,d\nu\right|.$$

For every $\delta>1/2$,

$$\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,N)\longrightarrow0$$

in probability under the true white-noise law $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$. This is a bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM conclusion; it asserts neither total-variation convergence on all Borel subsets nor an $L^2$-valued Gaussian limit.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The normal density is bounded and continuous, is bounded below by $(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-2}$ on $(-2,2)$, and has finite second moment $1$. The normalized truth coefficients all equal $r_{lk}=1$, hence $\sup_{l,k}|r_{lk}|=1\le M=1<\tau=2$.

The deterministic truth series is in $L^2$ because orthogonality gives $\sum_{l\ge0}\sum_{k\in K_l}\theta_{0,lk}^2=\sum_{l\ge0}2^l\sigma_l^2=\sum_{l\ge0}2^{-2\alpha l}<\infty$. The prior is likewise $L^2$-valued by [F1] under [A1].

All hypotheses of [F2] now hold, including continuity at each $r_{lk}=1$; therefore for every $\delta>1/2$ the scaled posterior converges to canonical white noise in the bounded-Lipschitz metric of $H(\delta)$.

Use the white-noise experiment, product prior, and supplied posterior kernel of [[thm-weak-nonparametric-bernstein-von-mises-for-product-priors]], with all its stated basis, coefficient-density, truth, and countable-choice hypotheses. Let $\Psi:L^2([0,1])\to\mathbb R$ be Borel measurable. Suppose $f_0\in L^2$, and for some $g\in H^s_2$, $s>1/2$, $g\ne0$, $C<\infty$, and $\rho>0$,
$$|\Psi(f_0+h)-\Psi(f_0)-\langle h,g\rangle_{L^2}|\le C\|h\|_2^2\quad\text{whenever }\|h\|_2\le\rho.$$
Assume the posterior contracts in $L^2$ at a deterministic radius $r_n=o(n^{-1/2})$, meaning $\Pi_n(\|f-f_0\|_2>r_n\mid X^{(n)})=o_{P_{f_0}^{(n)}}(1)$. Define the efficient center
$$\theta_n^*:=\Psi(f_0)+L_g(X^{(n)}-f_0),$$
where the last pairing is the continuous $H(\delta)$ extension from [[lem-smooth-functional-extends-to-negative-sobolev-space]]. Then the posterior law of $\sqrt n\{\Psi(f)-\theta_n^*\}$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance to $N(0,\|g\|_2^2)$ in $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$-probability. The equal-tailed posterior interval for $\Psi(f)$ at level $1-\alpha$ is credible and has frequentist coverage tending to $1-\alpha$.

The radius assumption is the stronger convention required by this plan. It implies the source's squared-radius condition: with $s_n=r_n^2$, one has $s_n=o(n^{-1/2})$ and posterior mass inside $\|f-f_0\|_2^2\le s_n$ tends to one.

derivations.claim: Expanding the inner product gives $\Psi(f_0+h)=\|f_0\|_2^2+2\langle f_0,h\rangle_{L^2}+\|h\|_2^2$. Thus the derivative is $D\Psi_{f_0}[h]=2\langle1,h\rangle_{L^2}$, which is nonzero, and the remainder equals $\|h\|_2^2$.

For $h_n=n^{-1/4}v$, $\|h_n\|_2=n^{-1/4}$ and $\sqrt n\|h_n\|_2^2=1$. Hence the scaled quadratic remainder does not tend to zero along this sequence, so the linear approximation needed in [F1] is not justified at this radius.

Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a countable complete orthonormal basis of the real Hilbert space $L^2([0,1])$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). For a wavelet basis, index levels by $l\ge0$, let $K_l$ have $2^l$ indices, and put $a_l=2^l$ for $l\ge1$ and $a_0=2$ for the finite coarsest level. This finite-level convention only prevents a zero logarithmic weight and does not change any convergence criterion below. For a trigonometric basis, use its integer frequency index $l$, bounded multiplicities, and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$.

Here an **$S$-regular wavelet basis** means a wavelet orthonormal basis whose members are $S$ times differentiable, with each derivative through order $S$ in $L^2([0,1])$, following the source convention. The weak BvM theorem below only uses the basis's completeness, orthonormality, and level counts.

For $\delta>0$, define $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ to be the space of coefficient sequences $c=(c_{lk})$ with norm

$$\|c\|_{H(\delta)}^2:=\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}|c_{lk}|^2<\infty.$$

Its inner product is the corresponding weighted coefficient inner product. Multiplying each coordinate by $a_l^{-1/2}(\log a_l)^{-\delta}$ identifies it isometrically with $\ell^2(I)$, where $I=\{(l,k):k\in K_l\}$ (or the corresponding trigonometric index set). This sequence space is complete: if $x^{(m)}$ is Cauchy, each coordinate converges to a scalar $x_i$; for every finite $F\subset I$, the Cauchy bound passes to the limit in $\sum_{i\in F}|x_i^{(m)}-x_i^{(n)}|^2$, so the supremum over finite $F$ shows $x^{(m)}\to x$ in $\ell^2(I)$. It is separable because finite-support sequences with rational coordinates form a countable dense set. Thus $H(\delta)$ is a separable Hilbert space without an additional choice assumption.

A function $f\in L^2([0,1])$ is identified with its coefficient sequence $c_{lk}=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$. For each finite set $F$ of indices, orthonormality makes $\sum_{(l,k)\in F}c_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ orthogonal to its residual in $L^2$, so the Pythagorean identity gives $\sum_F|c_{lk}|^2\le\|f\|_2^2$. Taking the supremum over finite $F$ and using the boundedness of the weights proves continuity of the coefficient map. If all coefficients of $f$ vanish, then $f$ is orthogonal to the linear span of the basis. Completeness makes this span dense, and continuity of $g\mapsto\langle f,g\rangle$ gives $\langle f,f\rangle=0$, hence $f=0$ in $L^2$. Applying this to the difference of two functions proves injectivity. Thus the coefficient map is a continuous linear embedding $L^2([0,1])\hookrightarrow H(\delta)$.

The weight trace $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}$ is finite exactly when $\delta>1/2$: for wavelets its tail is a constant multiple of $\sum_{l\ge1}l^{-2\delta}$, while for a trigonometric basis it is comparable to $\sum_{l\ge2}[l(\log l)^{2\delta}]^{-1}$. The product-prior theorem below uses the wavelet case.

Assume countable choice. Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the wavelet or trigonometric basis from [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. Let $Z_{lk}$ be mutually independent real random variables with density $g(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$. Define the formal white-noise coefficient sequence $W=(Z_{lk})$. For every $\delta>1/2$, this sequence is almost surely an element of $H(\delta)$ and is a Borel Gaussian random element there. Its law $N$ is a Borel probability on $H(\delta)$. For an infinite-dimensional basis, white noise is not an $L^2([0,1])$-valued random element. Here Gaussian means that each continuous real linear functional has a centered law $N(0,v)$ in the density convention of [[lem-density-normal-laws-and-square-summable-gaussian-series]]; in particular, for $L(c)=\sum_jd_jc_j$ its variance is $\sum_jd_j^2$ whenever this pairing is continuous on $H(\delta)$.
Assume AC. For $\delta>1/2$, the canonical white-noise law $N$ on the Polish space $H(\delta)$ from [[lem-white-noise-is-borel-gaussian-on-negative-sobolev-space]] is tight.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
